additional_concerns: Preservation of an existing application process does not expressly establish a substantive, permanent disqualification from relief. The legacy-exclusion readings remain proposed interpretations, not established consequences.

The introductory reference to immediate effect and the express 28 November 2025 commencement provision should be reconciled. The latter supports the selected date, but neither passage establishes a universal implementation-date test.
A transition fact fixed at commencement cannot resolve the effects of subsequent approval, withdrawal or resubmission. Candidates that use it to defeat relief indefinitely need further authority.
The substantive-only candidate deliberately leaves procedural availability unresolved. Its omission of application history is appropriate to its narrower question.
The two missing dependency IDs have no supplied mapping to named authorities. Neither can safely be identified as the FAQs or forms.
Home compliance and the exception classifications remain supplied judgments. The formulas do not establish those facts or determine the complete underlying approval obligation.
